"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/uncommon-words-from-two-sentences/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

884. Uncommon Words from Two Sentences

A sentence is a string of single-space separated words where each word consists only of lowercase letters.

A word is uncommon if it appears exactly once in one of the sentences, and does not appear in the other sentence.

Given two sentences s1 and s2, return a list of all the uncommon words. You may return the answer in any order.

Example 1:

Input: s1 = "this apple is sweet", s2 = "this apple is sour"
Output: ["sweet","sour"]
Explanation:
The word "sweet" appears only in s1, while the word "sour" appears only in s2.

Example 2:

Input: s1 = "apple apple", s2 = "banana"
Output: ["banana"]

Constraints:

    1 <= s1.length, s2.length <= 200
    s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters and spaces.
    s1 and s2 do not have leading or trailing spaces.
    All the words in s1 and s2 are separated by a single space.
"""


class Solution:
    def uncommonFromSentences(self, s1: str, s2: str) -> List[str]:
        from collections import Counter

        count1 = Counter(s1.split())
        count2 = Counter(s2.split())
        result = []
        for word in count1:
            if count1[word] == 1 and word not in count2:
                result.append(word)
        for word in count2:
            if count2[word] == 1 and word not in count1:
                result.append(word)
        return result


sol = Solution()

print(
    sol.uncommonFromSentences("this apple is sweet", "this apple is sour")
)  # ["sweet","sour"]

assert sorted(
    sol.uncommonFromSentences("this apple is sweet", "this apple is sour")
) == sorted(["sweet", "sour"])
assert sorted(sol.uncommonFromSentences("apple apple", "banana")) == sorted(["banana"])

assert sol.uncommonFromSentences("", "") == []
assert sol.uncommonFromSentences("a", "") == ["a"]
assert sol.uncommonFromSentences("", "b") == ["b"]
assert sol.uncommonFromSentences("a a a a a", "a") == []
assert (
    sol.uncommonFromSentences(
        "a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z",
        "z y x w v u t s r q p o n m l k j i h g f e d c b a",
    )
    == []
)
assert sol.uncommonFromSentences("apple banana apple", "banana orange orange") == []
assert sol.uncommonFromSentences("negative -1 -1 -2", "-2 -3 -3 -4") == [
    "negative",
    "-4",
]
assert sol.uncommonFromSentences("word " * 100, "unique") == ["unique"]
assert (
    sol.uncommonFromSentences(
        "one two three four five six seven eight nine ten " * 20,
        "ten nine eight seven six five four three two one " * 20,
    )
    == []
)
assert (
    sol.uncommonFromSentences(
        "repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat",
        "repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat repeat",
    )
    == []
)
assert (
    sol.uncommonFromSentences(
        "a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z " * 4,
        "z y x w v u t s r q p o n m l k j i h g f e d c b a " * 4,
    )
    == []
)
assert sol.uncommonFromSentences(
    "unique1 unique2 unique3", "unique4 unique5 unique6"
) == ["unique1", "unique2", "unique3", "unique4", "unique5", "unique6"]
